question: According to ICMR–NCDIR data, which of the following is the MOST common cancer in Indian males?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Colorectal cancer is not the leading cancer in Indian males; tobacco-related cancers dominate.
Correct. Oral cavity cancer (driven by tobacco and betel nut use) is the most common cancer in Indian males, reflecting the high prevalence of smokeless tobacco use.
Prostate cancer leads in Western males but is not the top cancer in Indian males.
Gastric cancer is more prevalent in South India but does not rank as the top cancer nationally in males.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the ICMR–NCDIR cancer burden data. Tobacco and betel nut use makes oral cavity cancer the leading cancer in Indian males.
Well done. India's tobacco epidemic makes oral cavity cancers the top cancer in males — this drives screening and primary prevention priorities.
